To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) rHVT- IBD vaccines are effective at inducing protection in SPF white leghorn and commercial broiler chickens; however, 2) the timing of the vaccine administration and IBDV challenge relative to the presence of anti-IBDV maternal antibodies in broilers is critical in determining the efficacy of these vaccines; and 3) rHVT vaccines can induce protection in broiler chickens at 30 and at 60 wk of broiler breeder age.

1) both rHVT+IBD vaccines were efficacious in SPF leghorn chicks, but 2) both rHVIT+IBD vaccines failed to protect 30-wk-old and 60-wk-old broiler progeny of an IBDV vaccinated breeder flock against challenge with a contemporary field strain of IBDV.

the efficacy of rHVT- IBD vaccines administered to broiler chicks from a single breeder flock at either 30 or 60 weeks of age was not as high as in SPF leghorn chicks, but both vaccines provided some protection against an IBD challenge in broilers.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Vaxxitec HVT+IBDV vaccine is more effective than the Vectormune Hvt-IBDV vaccine in protecting broiler chickens against IBDV challenge.
the rHVT- IBD vaccines were effective in reducing the incidence of IBD in broilers from 18 DPV onward.
both vaccines offer partial protection against IBD challenge in broiler progeny derived from a breeder flock vaccinated with an IBD vaccine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of rHVT- IBD vaccines in broiler chickens from a breeder flock vaccinated against IBDV may provide partial protection to broilers from an IBD challenge.
both vaccines are effective in controlling IBDV infection when administered to SPF leghorns.
the rHVT- IBD vaccines evaluated in this work were efficacious in protecting chickens from IBDV challenge when administered to chickens without anti-IBDV antibodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the window of susceptibility to IBDV exists between the wane of MDA and development of vaccine-induced antibody titers, and this window is not consistent across different commercial broiler strains.
the use of rHVT- IBD vaccines to control IBD in broilers may be more effective in younger broiler chicks, when MDA is at its highest levels, than in older broiler chickens.

the efficacy of rHVT- IBD vaccines in commercial poultry production may be affected by the timing of vaccination relative to the development of maternal antibodies and the age of the broiler chicken at the time of IBDV challenge.
